uniequip_002_yukari:
On the day off after the drama festival, the class president knocked at the dormitory door with an enormous tote bag in hand.
A short while later, in Yukari's room, Yukari in a Guard's uniform and Fuuka in a gunsmith's outfit stood before Amiya's camera.
"It looks great! I don't know how the teacher talked Closure into letting us keep these costumes." Amiya adjusted the framing, looking rather pleased.
Yukari and Fuuka glanced at each other and both broke into laughter. Fuuka straightened Yukari's cap and said, "You thought of that time too, didn't you, Yukari?" Amiya, who had been about to capture the two of them laughing, turned to look at them curiously.
Yukari waved a hand. "It's nothing—something from back in our world. Our school festival got canceled, so I dragged Fuuka into my room and we tried on the maid outfits we were supposed to wear for it."
"Those maid outfits were lovely too... but this Guard's uniform really suits you, Yukari, with your archery." said Fuuka.
Amiya, watching the two of them through the viewfinder, said suddenly, "Actually... this is only hypothetical, but if you stayed in Laterano, I think you'd fit right into the Guard, Yukari."
"Huh...? Can foreigners even do that?" Yukari tilted her head, curious.
"Sankta who have returned home can. The teacher seems to know someone like that. And if others could obtain Lateran citizenship, then probably yes? ...It's all hypothetical anyway. I just thought it would suit you." Amiya answered, capturing the shot of Yukari with her head tilted.
Yukari grew thoughtful. "Come to think of it, the Guard I played was originally just a pilgrim... In the last scene, when she stands on the wall looking out over all of Laterano, the narration says that coming this far was 'fate's reward'—that must mean her becoming a member of the Guard, too."
"So that character became a Guard because fate willed it..." Fuuka said, though her expression carried a trace of sorrow.
"Ah, I don't think it's like that... What I mean is, that character must have put in enough effort to earn that reward at the end." Yukari went on, "If fate could decide our futures however it pleased, wouldn't that be awful? What would all our effort even be for? If someone told me, 'the festival being canceled by a typhoon was fate's arrangement,' I wouldn't want to just accept that."
Amiya listened to the two of them and fell silent. If this meeting with them was fate's reward, then the reward was fleeting and insubstantial. When the friends before her returned to their own world, would they even remember this place... The teacher had said that once they went back they might forget it all, that the severed causality between worlds would smooth away the ripples of information. What does a compensation that is destined to be forgotten actually compensate for?
Yukari looked out the window. It was a beautiful clear day, and a fowlbeast was gliding lightly past the tops of the buildings.
"Just like that pilgrim said herself—be honest with your heart, do what is right, and you'll meet the one you've been hoping for somewhere along the road... That's what fate is, and that's what deserves to be called a reward."
A bright smile spread across her face, and Fuuka caught it from her. Amiya, looking at their smiling faces, gave a small, firm nod.
